title: The conversation before the door closes
text: You and {partner.first}, both adults, have a quiet evening alone. Desire is easy to name; boundaries and expectations take more courage.

choices.label: Talk honestly about what you both want

outcomes.text: We agreed on what felt right. The night stayed private, and we felt closer.
We wanted different things. We stopped, talked, and kept each other’s trust.
We shared an unhurried evening without pushing further. Nobody had to prove anything.
It was a little awkward, but we laughed and agreed to talk again.

choices.label: Say you would rather stop tonight

outcomes.text: My boundary was respected. The evening ended gently.
Disappointment was real, but stopping was still the right choice for me.

title: What we remember about that night
text: The private evening is long past. What remains is how you made room for each other’s boundaries.

outcomes.text: We found words for something we had both carried quietly.
The conversation was difficult, but it made the next one easier.
We protected an evening from the rest of our responsibilities.
Life interrupted our plans. We made another date instead of blaming each other.
I understood my own boundaries more clearly.
I realised a conversation I had avoided was still waiting.

title: A message you should not answer
text: An adult acquaintance sends a flirtatious invitation. You have a partner. There is no misunderstanding about what is being offered.

outcomes.text: I declined. The invitation stopped there.
They called me boring. I could live with that.

choices.label: Talk to your partner before doing anything

outcomes.text: We had a hard conversation about what was missing between us.
Honesty exposed problems we could no longer pretend away.
The thrill was real. So was the lie I carried home.
We crossed the boundary, and my partner learned about it soon after.

title: The invitation leaves a mark
text: That invitation changed how you think about loyalty. The consequences did not end with deleting a message.

outcomes.text: I took responsibility for my choices instead of arguing about how they looked.
There was no quick forgiveness. I accepted that repair takes time.

choices.label: Invest in the relationship you want

outcomes.text: Counselling and time helped me become more honest.
Money did not solve the tension, but the work gave us a place to start.
Silence made every disagreement feel larger.
The old uncertainty followed me into a new argument.

title: A message after a private night
text: Someone you were intimate with as an adult says they may have a sexually transmitted infection. They ask you to get tested. Nothing about the message is a diagnosis.

outcomes.text: I got professional advice and a plan for testing. Uncertainty was easier with help.
The appointment did not answer everything immediately. I followed the clinician’s plan.

choices.label: Tell current adult partners and seek advice

outcomes.text: The conversation was uncomfortable, but we could make informed choices together.
Someone was frightened. We chose facts and clinical advice over blame.
I avoided an awkward appointment and kept worrying.
Delaying care made the uncertainty harder to manage.

title: Care is a continuing choice
text: The private health concern is no longer new. Follow-through and honest communication still matter.

outcomes.text: I completed the recommended follow-up and felt steadier.
I needed another visit. Having a plan helped.

choices.label: Check in with the people affected

outcomes.text: We spoke respectfully about boundaries and care.
The conversation was difficult, but nobody was left guessing.
The worry stayed with me longer than I expected.
I eventually had to face the concern I had avoided.

title: A price on someone’s life
text: A criminal contact offers money if you help arrange the murder of an adult rival. They speak about a person as if they were a business expense.

outcomes.text: I walked away. The contact stopped calling.
Refusing cost me the contact’s trust. Keeping it would have cost more.

choices.label: Seek legal help and report the threat

outcomes.text: I gave a statement with legal support. An investigation began.
Reporting brought difficult questions, but the intended victim received a warning.
A person died because of the decision I made. Investigators traced my involvement; I was convicted.
The plan was intercepted. I was convicted for my role in the attempted murder.

title: The offer that will not stay in the past
text: The murder plot changed lives. Whether you refused, reported it, or participated, its shadow remains.

outcomes.text: I gave a truthful account. It did not erase what happened.
The interview reopened old fear. I answered with legal support.

choices.label: Seek support and face your responsibility

outcomes.text: I began the slow work of living honestly with my choices.
Support helped me function. It did not turn the past into something harmless.

choices.label: Pretend it has nothing to do with you

outcomes.text: Denial made it harder to speak honestly to anyone.
A new question pulled me straight back into the memory.

title: What you saw after midnight
text: You witness the aftermath of a fatal attack on an adult outside a club. A familiar adult asks you to say they were somewhere else.

outcomes.text: I described only what I knew. My statement became part of the investigation.
I corrected a detail rather than guessing. The investigators needed honesty, not a perfect story.

choices.label: Get a lawyer before making a statement

outcomes.text: Legal advice helped me separate facts from fear.
The waiting was miserable, but I gave a careful statement with support.
My lie was contradicted by other evidence. I was convicted of obstructing the investigation.
The lie held for now. I knew an innocent person might bear the cost.

title: The statement is read aloud
text: The fatal attack has become a court case. Someone reads the statement you gave, and your choices return in public.

choices.label: Clarify the truth with legal support

outcomes.text: I corrected the record. It was painful and necessary.
The court questioned every change. I kept to what I actually knew.
I offered practical help without making their grief about me.
They wanted distance. I respected it.
The case stayed on the news. Avoidance was not an ending.
I could stop reading, but I could not stop remembering.

title: Pay up, or everyone finds out
text: Someone threatens to publish private, consensual adult messages unless you pay. Their demand is an act of exploitation, not a debt you owe.

choices.label: Seek support and report the threat

outcomes.text: I asked for help and preserved what I could safely share with investigators.
The process was slow. Having someone on my side made it bearable.

choices.label: Tell the people who could be affected

outcomes.text: A painful conversation took some power away from the threat.
Not everyone reacted kindly. I still had support from someone I trusted.
I paid $2,000. The demand returned with a larger number.
The messages stopped for now. I had bought uncertainty, not safety.

title: The threat comes back
text: A reminder of the extortion arrives. You have another chance to choose support over isolation.

outcomes.text: I made a supported plan instead of answering alone.
The problem was not instantly solved, but I had a clear next step.
I was believed. That mattered more than a clever reply.
Talking was hard. Keeping the secret had been harder.
Every notification made me flinch.
I spent another year arranging my life around someone else’s threat.

title: An envelope without a receipt
text: A supplier offers a private payment if you steer a contract their way. They call it appreciation. The contract team calls it a conflict of interest.

outcomes.text: I reported the offer. The review delayed the project but protected the process.
Someone complained that I made trouble. I kept a clear record of my decision.
I handed the decision to an independent colleague.
The supplier tried again elsewhere. My withdrawal did not end the concern.
The $5,000 felt easy until the audit began.
The offer was part of an investigation. I was convicted of bribery.

title: The audit asks one more question
text: The contract is being reviewed. The question is no longer whether the project looked successful, but who benefited.

outcomes.text: I answered directly and accepted scrutiny.
Cooperation exposed a decision I regretted. I stopped making excuses.
Advice helped me respond carefully and honestly.
There was no painless route through the review.
The accusation damaged my credibility when the records contradicted it.
I kept my position for now, but people stopped trusting me.

title: Different rules, honest answers
text: Your adult partner asks whether a consensually non-monogamous relationship could work for you both. An honest no is as valid as an honest yes.

outcomes.text: We agreed on rules, check-ins and the freedom to change our minds.
The discussion showed that we needed different things. We chose not to rush.
I stated what I needed. My partner respected the answer.
Our needs differed. We had a difficult but honest conversation.
We paused the decision and talked without pressure.
Uncertainty was uncomfortable, but I refused to promise what I did not mean.

title: Checking the agreement
text: Whatever relationship rules you chose, they only work when everyone can speak freely about them.

choices.label: Check whether the agreement still works

outcomes.text: We adjusted expectations before resentment grew.
A boundary had changed. We took it seriously.
Naming jealousy made it easier to discuss without accusation.
There was no easy answer, but the feeling was heard.
Resentment seeped into unrelated arguments.
I realised silence had become its own decision.

title: A bill with no good answer
text: A friend needs urgent help with a debt. A fixer offers to erase it if you help conceal money from an illegal operation.

outcomes.text: A slow payment plan gave my friend room to breathe.
There was no immediate rescue. I helped with the practical work anyway.

choices.label: Refuse the scheme but stay beside your friend

outcomes.text: I could not fix the debt, but I did not abandon them.
They were angry. Later, they understood why I had refused.
The debt disappeared. A new obligation to the fixer took its place.
The transaction was investigated. I was convicted of money laundering.

title: The price of the favour
text: Your friend’s crisis changed the limits you thought you had. The favour still has a price, even if the bill looks different now.

outcomes.text: I began unpicking obligations with professional help.
The route was slow, but it stopped adding new lies.
We stopped treating the problem as a secret test of loyalty.
Honesty changed the friendship. It was overdue.
Every favour made the next refusal harder.
I had become useful to people who did not care what it cost me.

title: Opportunity with a condition attached
text: A senior colleague implies an adult promotion opportunity depends on private sexual attention. This is pressure from someone with power, not a genuine choice of equal partners.

outcomes.text: I refused and spoke to an independent adviser. The process was stressful, but I was not alone.
Refusing made work awkward. Support helped me plan the next step.
An inquiry began. I was asked difficult questions with support available.
The organisation handled it badly. I looked for advice beyond the workplace.

choices.label: Seek another role and protect your boundaries

outcomes.text: I chose distance from the pressure and began applying elsewhere.
Leaving the opportunity hurt. Keeping my boundaries mattered more.

title: What a safe workplace would mean
text: The pressure at work made you reconsider who gets to set the conditions of opportunity.

outcomes.text: I found people who took the concern seriously.
Progress was slow. I kept control of what I chose to share.
I listened without telling them what they had to do.
I helped them find independent advice and respected their choices.

choices.label: Focus on rebuilding your own life

outcomes.text: A healthier routine gave me some room back.
Recovery was uneven, but I could make choices for myself again.
